Guides

Spoon, fingers, or both

Purées, finger foods, or a mix of both can all feed a baby well. The debate about which camp you’re in is louder than the evidence.

Findings

Iron, texture, and following your baby’s cues matter more than the method. You can spoon-feed, let your baby feed themselves soft pieces, or do both in the same week.
In a trial that taught safe shapes, finger foods didn’t increase choking. Gagging was common. Choking wasn’t more common when families were shown which shapes to avoid.
Smooth food has a use-by date. By eight or nine months, a baby should be moving on to mashed food and soft pieces. Staying on thin purée is a risk you can avoid.

Three ways that work

Spoon-feeding lets you offer iron-rich meat and lentils in a smooth form while chewing is still new. Finger foods let your baby practise gripping and set their own pace. Most families end up mixing the two, and that’s a proper method in its own right, not a compromise.

As a slogan, baby-led weaning sometimes forgets iron, or keeps meals so simple that the baby fills up on fruit. The studies that found baby-led feeding safe told families to include iron-rich foods and to avoid round, hard, and coin-shaped pieces.

What the BLISS trial showed

New Zealand’s BLISS trial (Baby-Led Introduction to Solids) compared supported baby-led feeding with usual spoon-feeding. There was no sign of more choking. Gagging, which is noisy and protective, was a normal part of learning.

That doesn’t mean every hard shop-bought biscuit is safe. It means soft strips, flakes of fish, and well-cooked vegetables, offered to a baby sitting upright, carried about the same risk as spoon-feeding.

Keep moving the texture on

At first, food can be smooth or naturally soft. By about eight months, move to mash with soft lumps and pieces your baby can hold in their fist. By about a year, they should be eating family textures, with their portion still unsalted.

You don’t need a blender. A fork will mash banana, avocado, and the soft inside of baked vegetables. Blenders whip air into food; if your baby seems windy afterwards, stir the purée and let it stand for a bit before serving.
